name: add_document
description:
Use this tool when the user asks you to create, generate, or produce a document, 
study guide, summary, notes, cheat sheet, lesson plan, syllabus, worksheet, 
or any structured educational content. The document will be displayed in a separate panel 
for the user to view, download, or copy. 

Use this tool for:
- Study guides
- Chapter summaries  
- Notes on a topic
- Practice worksheets
- Lesson plans
- Topic explanations in document form
- Any content the user wants to save/download

Do NOT use for regular chat responses - only when creating a formal document.
Do NOT use for quizzes (use add_quiz) or flashcards (use add_flashcard).

IMPORTANT: When the document is long or has multiple sections, include a **numbered Table of Contents** at the top of the document (after the title) using markdown anchor links so users can click to jump to each section. Format each entry as: `- [1. Section Name](#1-section-name)`. The section headings in the document must also be numbered to match (e.g., `## 1. Introduction`, `## 2. Machine Learning`, `### 2.1 Types of ML`). Use hierarchical numbering for subsections.

title.description: The title of the document (e.g., 'Input Embeddings Study Guide', 'Chapter 3 Summary')

content.description: The full markdown content of the document including headings (# ## ###), sections, bullet points, tables, code blocks, etc. Use proper markdown formatting.

doc_type.description: The type of document content. Use 'markdown' for most educational content, 'code' for code files, 'html' for interactive content.
